newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian stocks poised to shoot higher at yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian stocks poised to shoot higher at yr-end.

text.p: Brazilian stocks are poised for further gains by year's end as fair prospects for bellwether Telebras continue to feed this year's rally, analysts said.

"The market today is backed by positive earnings prospects for the main share traded: Telebras," said Luis Eduardo de Assis, director of Investments Management at Citibank Brazil, which manages $4.5 billion in clients' assets.
Between January and August, Telebras preferred rose 61.93 percent, outshining even the 45.6 percent rise in the Bovespa index of the 49 most-traded shares in the same period.

Assis also said the market has become much less sensitive to political and macroeconomic news as traders now have faith in the stability of the economy. "Previously, the market chased a lot of news. This no longer happens," he said.
The market this year was expected to forge ahead on optimism over congressional approval of key constitutional reforms, including pension and administrative reforms, analysts said.

Although prices are currently snagged in a narrow range, experts are bullish on the market's prospects as the year draws to a close. They have an especially positive view on Telebras, which accounts for over 70 percent of Sao Paulo bourse's total trade.
The firm is expected to post earnings of at least 2.2 billion reais by the end of 1996, almost three times last year's earnings, analysts said.

And some believe the privatization has not yet been fully priced in. "Telebras still owes us a rise that corresponds to the company's perspectives in light of privatization," said Renato Tranjan of Rio-based Banco Omega.
The Communications Ministry expects the telecom sector to be fully privatized by the end of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's term on January 1, 1999.
Analysts project Telebras preferred will reach $95 to $100 by year's end, an increase of about 27 percent from the stock's current $78.50 price. In New York, Telebras's ADR traded at 79-1/8.
But as reform legislation became mired ahead of October's municipal elections, the stock market has turned its attention to other factors.
"U.S. interest rates began to have more of an impact," said a fund manager at a local investment bank who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Brazilian analysts have expressed concern over a possible hike in U.S. rates which would dash hopes of an increase in foreign capital inflows to the local market.
"The international outlook determines whether or not foreign capital comes in," said Citibank's Assis.
But fears of a significant rate hike are fading before the September 24 meeting of the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee.
"We do not expect any disaster in terms of U.S. rates," said another fund manager at a foreign bank.
Analysts also said optimism over the privatization of the power sector and mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce would continue bolstering market sentiment.
The sell-off of Eletrobras' major assets is expected to begin by the end of 1997, while Vale is scheduled to be privatized in February next year.
